distinguishing_features: Infers thermal fatigue accumulation of a bladder from pressure-flow hysteresis energy (∮PdV) of the pressurization curve, rather than a tube-leak's effective orifice area from transient pressure-coupling decay constant
Uses cumulative cyclic hysteresis-loop area growth as a degradation-accumulation metric predicting crack initiation, rather than instantaneous leak conductance inference
Applies to rubber/composite bladder bead fatigue under curing cycles rather than shell-and-tube heat-exchanger leakage
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to predict incipient thermal-fatigue crack initiation at a bladder bead before visible damage, using only existing pressure and flow signals.
parsed.viable_reason: The physics is internally inconsistent — hysteresis loop area grows with viscoelastic loss, but the stated 15% area change is asserted from unrelated da/dN kinetics without a valid scaling bridge, and an absolute loop area of 0.5 J/m³ cannot be discriminated against sensor noise at 1.5 MPa, so the mechanism is not credibly testable as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Deriving pre-failure fatigue state from pressure-flow hysteresis rather than direct leak detection is a genuine conceptual departure from the closest art, not a routine parameter tweak.
